CFML Language Reference: Functions

DateCompare

Tells you whether the first date is earlier than (-1), equal to (0) or later than (1) the second date. An optional third argument sets how precisely to compare.

Category

Date and time functions

Syntax

DateCompare(date1, date2 [, datePart ])

Parameters

date1
A date/time value or a string that can be converted to one.
date2
A date/time value or a string that can be converted to one.
datePart
Optional precision: yyyy year, m month, d day, h hour, n minute or s second. Default s. The comparison ignores everything smaller than this unit. Other datepart strings compare to the second.

Returns

-1 if date1 is earlier, 0 if they are the same (at the chosen precision), 1 if date1 is later.

Usage

Comparing by day is the easy way to ask "is this the same day?" without worrying about the clock: DateCompare(Posted, Now(), "d") EQ 0. Date values can also be compared directly with LT, GT and EQ in an expression.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET A = CreateDateTime(1999, 12, 31, 10, 0, 0)>
<CFSET B = CreateDateTime(1999, 12, 31, 18, 30, 0)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<P>A = #A#<BR>B = #B#</P>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Precision</TH><TH>DateCompare(A, B, ...)</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP INDEX="Part" LIST="s,n,h,d,m,yyyy">
<TR><TD>#Part#</TD><TD>#DateCompare(A, B, Part)#</TD></TR>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<P>DateCompare(B, A) = #DateCompare(B, A)#</P>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

DateDiff, DateAdd, IsDate, Now
